crop.notes: Whole article from the headline 'THE COMING PRIZE FIGHT. Attempt to Assassinate Bill Davis', plus the following 'PUGILISTIC' item on the same subject, to the end of the dog-fight line.

ocr.notes: Matches the image closely; the 'PUGILISTIC.—' heading is omitted, and the image reads 'reduced 25 pounds' (not 26).

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported that on Christmas night 1868 rowdies said to be Allen's backers attacked Bill Davis at Doyle's near the Fair Grounds, cutting his wrist with a knife, weeks before his fight with Tom Allen.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The Missouri Republican—St. Louis, December 28, 1868'. The paper itself mixes up the hometowns ('Bill Davis, of St. Louis, and Tom Allen, of California').

facts.fact: Seven or eight rowdies said to be backers of Allen attacked Bill Davis at Doyle's, his training quarters near the Fair Grounds, on Christmas night; one drew a knife and cut Davis on the wrist
places: Doyle's, near the Fair Grounds, St. Louis

notes: The link to Allen's backers is only 'said to be'; Davis's own account (article 006) does not name who was behind it.
